decisions.statement: The page type is read from the path the change is handed.
A path naming no page type is refused here.
A property the page type carries nowhere is refused here.
The declaration written is the one the page type's own body states.
The pages written are the pages of that page type and of every page type beneath it.
Which pages state the property is read from the values the index files.
The declaration and every page under it are answered in this one answer.
A page stating no value gains the default where the property becomes required.
A page stating no value is refused where the property becomes required and no default is stated.
A page stating one value in a list has that list unwrapped where the declaration holds one.
A page stating a value outside a list has that value wrapped where the declaration holds many.
A page whose list holds other than one value is refused where the declaration holds one.
A count is written on the declaration where it holds many and taken off where it holds one.
A refusal names the page that drew the refusal.
No rung beneath is reached.
A default is written on the declaration and gained by a page stating no value.
A default is spelled as text on the declaration and as its own kind on a page.
A default the property's kind cannot hold is refused.
A declaration holding many values is refused a default.
A default is taken off the declaration where the caller states none.

definition: a page type's declaration of one property stated anew, with its pages carried to match
